title: Grindlemost the Quartering Slagling
story: In the cinder pits below the old mint, Grindlemost the Quartering Slagling guards a stolen coin-mold — and every time it is struck, each slagling bursts into 4 smaller sluggish ones. Mr 6 starts with 1 slagling and knows that striking is a trap, so he counts carefully first. He learns that any pile of slaglings will crawl harmlessly into a cooling trench once there are more than 200 of them, because they get in each other's way.
question: If Mr 6 strikes every slagling once per round, how many slaglings will there be after 4 rounds?
solution: Each round multiplies the number of slaglings by 4: 1 -> 4 -> 16 -> 64.
One more round: 64 * 4 = 256 slaglings after round 4.
So after 4 rounds there are 256 slaglings — just past the 200 needed.
praise: Multiplying by 4 each round was exactly right — it just needed one more round of quadrupling to reach round 4.
hint: Write the count after each round: start at 1, then multiply by 4, and do that four times in a row.
victory: The 256 slaglings jam together like coins in a too-small purse and tumble, clinking, into the cooling trench. Mr 6 picks up the coin-mold and remarks that sometimes the smartest way to beat a crowd is to invite one.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight standing calmly on a ledge above a glowing cinder pit, counting on his fingers as a tide of tiny molten slag creatures splits into fours and tumbles into a steaming trench.
